# Issue review

## Scope

Relevance pass over the whole offline backlog in [`.github/issues/`](../issues) — **499 files** — plus a completeness check of that dump against GitHub. Every verdict for an open issue was derived from the code on `main` during this pass; closed issues were re-checked against GitHub for status and state reason, and sampled in the code where the closure carried a claim worth testing.

Reviewed revision: `main` at `a732d78` (*fix #877: zsh: drop the unused docker and kubectl plugins, they raced compinit*, 2026-09-16), with the uncommitted rewrite of `.github/issues/` in the working tree — that working-tree content is what was reviewed.

This document is also the new home of the per-issue state notes. Until this pass every issue file carried a **Current state** paragraph describing what the repository does today. That is a property of the code, not of the request: it ages on a different clock from the description, it duplicates the `status` field, and it turns a task into a report. The descriptions were reduced to intent — what is wanted and why — and the state was moved here, where it can be dated, superseded and re-run as a whole.

Vocabulary. **Relevant** means work remains; priority is not assessed. **Defect confirmed** means the fault was located in the code during this pass and the file and line are given. **Partial** means part of the expected behaviour exists. **Needs clarification** means there is not enough evidence either to close the issue or to start implementation. **No longer relevant** means the request has been met, has been overtaken, or has lost the condition that motivated it — it is not a statement that the work was done. In the table below the **Assessment** cell always opens with one of these five terms — *Defect confirmed*, *Relevant*, *Partial*, *No longer relevant*, *Needs clarification* — and any qualifier follows an em dash, so the column both reads and counts.

## Dump integrity

The dump is **complete and, with two exceptions, accurate**.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Files vs. issues | 499 local files, 499 issues on GitHub; no file without an issue, no issue without a file |
| `title` | 499 of 499 agree |
| `labels` | 499 of 499 agree |
| `status` | 497 of 499 agree |
| `updated_at` | 497 of 499 agree |

The two exceptions are the same two issues:

| Issue | Local | GitHub | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#873](../issues/DOT-498.md) | `open` | `closed` (completed), `2026-09-08T12:12:09Z` | `fix #873` landed after the dump was taken |
| [#877](../issues/DOT-499.md) | `open` | `closed` (completed), `2026-09-16T18:45:55Z` | closed by `a732d78`, the reviewed `HEAD` itself |

So the live split is **116 open / 383 closed**, not the 118 / 381 the front matter reports. Of the 383 closed, GitHub records 380 as `completed` and 3 as `not planned` — [#242](../issues/DOT-241.md), [#402](../issues/DOT-399.md), [#724](../issues/DOT-486.md) — a distinction the dump's front matter cannot express.

One further staleness, of a kind the table cannot catch: the state note for [#114](../issues/DOT-113.md) recorded the zsh plugin list as `(common-aliases docker docker-compose git golang kubectl)`. `a732d78` removed two of those plugins the day after the note was written. It is the clearest argument for keeping state out of the issue files: the note was correct when written, wrong a day later, and nothing linked it to the commit that invalidated it.

**Reconciled after this pass.** On 2026-09-17, once the descriptions above had been accepted, the dump and GitHub were synchronised in both directions and the two exceptions in the table are gone. Bodies went local to GitHub — all 499, the issue body being the file below the front matter, without the `# <title>` heading, which duplicates `title`, and without the trailing note blocks, which live as comments; the only rewrites were the links that a GitHub body cannot resolve, `[#114](DOT-113.md)` becoming the autolink `#114` (266 of them) and `[tools.go](../../toolset/tools.go)` becoming a `blob/main` URL (163 of them). Metadata went the other way: `status` for the two issues above, and `updated_at` for all 499, because every push moves it. `title` and `labels` already agreed and were not touched. A fresh read of the API afterwards reports no mismatch in body, title, labels, status or updated_at, and the comment mirror still stands at 219 against 219 across 178 issues. What this does not change: the verdicts below were formed against the descriptions as they are, and the state they describe is the state of `a732d78`.

## Validation and sources

Everything below was checked against `main` at `a732d78` during this pass, on macOS 26.6 with zsh 5.9.2.

- Dump integrity was established by comparing every local file's front matter with the GitHub API (issues only, pull requests excluded), field by field, for all 499 issues.
- Alias registration was compared between [`bin/git_config`](../../bin/git_config) and [`bin/legacy/git`](../../bin/legacy/git). `git_config` registers 20 aliases; `bin/legacy/git` registers 24, of which 22 are not in `git_config`, among them `refresh`, `shake`, `untag`, `mirror`, `url`, `root`, `stats`, `delta`, `whoami`, `branches`, `aliases`, `configure` and `flow`. Nothing runs `bin/legacy/git`, so on any machine configured after the 2022 alias refactoring those commands do not exist.
- `bin/git_shake:27-28` was read directly: the remote sweep splits `remote/branch` with `${target//\// }` and `awk`, and the `was deleted` message follows the push unconditionally.
- `bin/lib/git/sync.bash:9` passes an explicit `--tags` to `git pull`, and `:22` pushes `--tags` to every non-fork remote.
- `bin/self-update` was read for the three findings carried from the 2026 reviews: `eval "${update}"` at `:133`, `rm -rf "${HOME}"/go/bin/*` at `:73`, `git reset --hard` at `:136`, with `ensure_clean` at `:96` guarding the start of the run but not changes the run itself creates.
- `install` was read for the four findings of the July 2026 reviews: top-level `return 0` at `:19` and `:125`, the Command Line Tools check at `:34`, `compaudit | xargs chmod` at `:144`.
- `bin/git_current:34,37` uses `grep -v '[:alpha:]'` — a bracket expression, not a character class — so the release-tag filter drops any tag containing `:`, `a`, `l`, `p` or `h`.
- `bin/lib/sys.bash` includes `clone`, `debug`, `path` and `strings` only; [`bin/lib/sys/sign-in.bash`](../../bin/lib/sys/sign-in.bash) is never stitched in, so the `sign-in` function does not exist in any shell.
- `bin/lib/aliases.bash:62-64` defines `oom` inside `if ! command -v journalctl`, i.e. precisely where it cannot work.
- `config/zsh/.zshrc` was read for [#189](../issues/DOT-188.md), [#600](../issues/DOT-464.md) and [#114](../issues/DOT-113.md): `ZSH_THEME=agnoster`, `zstyle ':omz:update' mode disabled`, `plugins=(common-aliases docker-compose git golang)`.
- The Brewfiles were read for every tooling verdict: a common [`Brewfile`](../../toolset/Brewfile) of nine formulae and two casks, plus three host files and [`candidates.Brewfile`](../../toolset/custom/candidates.Brewfile). `raycast` and `warp` are on all three hosts; `grpcurl` on two; `gum`, `composer`, `ngrok` and `zotero` are in the candidates only, which means `self-update brew` removes them.
- `bin/lib/git/commit.bash` was read for [#609](../issues/DOT-468.md) (`init the repository` at `:76,79`), [#433](../issues/DOT-416.md) (`--target`, default 25) and [#377](../issues/DOT-376.md) (the `cannot suggest a timestamp` guard at `:50`).
- `test/lookup.bats` still asserts `git_commit`, `bin/explain`, `git_aliases` and the `m`/`mm` aliases, none of which exist; `bin/git_aliases` is gone from the tree.
- Eighteen `git_*` scripts remain in [`bin`](../../bin), two of which (`git_lock`, `git_unlock`) were added in 2025.

The issue descriptions were not consulted as evidence about the code; every claim above was read from the source.

| [#630](../issues/DOT-477.md) | Notify when a run exceeds a threshold | Relevant — design settled | `bin/notify` reserves `notify run …` for this and exits 2, so the shape is decided; the timing and the notification call remain to be written. |

| [#638](../issues/DOT-479.md) | Recognise `.venv` as well as `.virtenv` | Relevant — four places | `activate`, the `v@`/`v+` aliases and the global gitignore all name `.virtenv` only. |

| [#665](../issues/DOT-483.md) | Investigate ShellHistory | Relevant — duplicate question | Not installed, no shell hook. It asks the same question as #664 with a different answer; the two should be decided together, not separately. |
| [#709](../issues/DOT-484.md) | Publish the Brewfile | No longer relevant — as written | "My Brewfile" is now a minimal common file plus three host files plus an unfiltered candidates dump, so there is no single artefact to publish without first deciding what it should contain. |
| [#720](../issues/DOT-485.md) | Tools from a later batch of reviews | Relevant | None of Starship, the zsh plugins, go-task or `just` is declared. Two of the videos bear on this repository's own choice of task runner, which makes it more than a shopping list. |

Secrets, the piece the source material adds, remain absent although the 1Password CLI is installed. |

The consuming hook lives in another repository, so the end-to-end behaviour cannot be verified from here and never will be. |

### Closures that today's code does not back

These are closed, and the code does not support the closure. None of them is a reason to reopen by itself — several are better absorbed by an open ticket — but each is a claim the repository no longer honours.

| Issue | Closed as | What the code says |

| [#114](../issues/DOT-113.md) | zsh plugins for golang, git, kubectl enabled | `a732d78` removed the `kubectl` and `docker` plugins as the cause of a `compinit` race. Two of the three are gone by design; the completions now come from Homebrew. |
| [#131](../issues/DOT-130.md) | ngrok installed with token support | The token half is `sign-in` in `bin/lib/sys/sign-in.bash`, which `bin/lib/sys.bash` does not include, so the function is never defined. The cask is in the candidates only. Dead code either way. |
| [#169](../issues/DOT-168.md) | version tag preferred when several point at the same commit | `bin/git_current:34,37` filters with `grep -v '[:alpha:]'`, a bracket expression matching the five literal characters, not the alphabetic class. The selection is wrong for any tag containing one of them. |
| [#67](../issues/DOT-66.md) | `oom` alias added | `bin/lib/aliases.bash:62` defines it only when `journalctl` is **absent**, i.e. on macOS, where the command it wraps does not exist. |
| [#19](../issues/DOT-19.md) | `git aliases` pretty-printer added | `bin/git_aliases` no longer exists, and the alias survives only in `bin/legacy/git`, so it would fail even if it were registered. |

On a machine set up after 2022 none of these commands exists. This is the same systemic gap that [#355](../issues/DOT-354.md) and [#356](../issues/DOT-355.md)–[#361](../issues/DOT-360.md) are about. |
| [#206](../issues/DOT-205.md) | Homebrew permission problems fixed | `install:144` ends with `compaudit` piped into `xargs chmod g-w,o-w`, annotated *not tested in the whole installation process*. `compaudit` is a zsh builtin; in a bash script the pipeline fails, which is the July 2026 review's finding 2. |
| [#258](../issues/DOT-257.md) | installer extended with `xcode-select` | `install:34` returns as soon as `command -v xcode-select` succeeds. macOS always ships that binary, so the installation step is skipped on exactly the machines that need it. |
| [#787](../issues/DOT-490.md) | broken installation script fixed | The typo was fixed; the top-level `return 0` at `install:19` and `:125` was not, and it aborts the installer rather than ending it. |
| [#154](../issues/DOT-153.md) | bats-core integrated for unit testing | The submodules are there and Dependabot keeps them current, but `test/lookup.bats` asserts four things that no longer exist, so the suite documents a 2021 tree. ## Recommendations

Ordered by how much they change the state of the backlog.

1. **Refresh the dump for [#873](../issues/DOT-498.md) and [#877](../issues/DOT-499.md).** Both are closed on GitHub; the local front matter says otherwise. Everything else in the dump agrees with the API field for field, so this is the only correction it needs.
2. **Close the fourteen issues whose condition has gone.** Each has lost the thing that motivated it, not merely gone stale: [#151](../issues/DOT-150.md) (Composer is installed nowhere), [#189](../issues/DOT-188.md) (the update prompt is disabled in `.zshrc`), [#196](../issues/DOT-195.md) (superseded by `--fixup`/`--autosquash`), [#288](../issues/DOT-287.md) (Git's `:/` pathspec does it), [#351](../issues/DOT-350.md) (no iTerm2 on the hosts, Warp does it natively), [#398](../issues/DOT-396.md) (osxc unmaintained since ~2017), [#480](../issues/DOT-436.md) (four years, no outcome, fully covered by its siblings), [#494](../issues/DOT-440.md) (the portability argument died with Linux support), [#500](../issues/DOT-442.md) (ngrok is no longer installed, so there is nothing to replace), [#513](../issues/DOT-446.md) (Raycast ships window management on all three hosts), [#585](../issues/DOT-463.md) (an umbrella whose every actionable part became its own ticket), [#609](../issues/DOT-468.md) (done but for a part that belongs to [#173](../issues/DOT-172.md)), [#709](../issues/DOT-484.md) (there is no single Brewfile to publish any more), [#861](../issues/DOT-497.md) (the described PoC is merged; the other half lives in another repository and always will).

   Two more belong in this group only if the author agrees with the premise: [#128](../issues/DOT-127.md), which assumes a Bitbucket mirror workflow that nothing in the repository still exercises, and [#239](../issues/DOT-238.md), whose three concrete cases each became a ticket of its own, leaving a mechanism with no case to justify it.
3. **Merge the nine duplicate pairs before doing anything else with them.** [#136](../issues/DOT-135.md) into [#605](../issues/DOT-467.md); [#145](../issues/DOT-144.md) into [#471](../issues/DOT-434.md); [#226](../issues/DOT-225.md) into [#138](../issues/DOT-137.md); [#234](../issues/DOT-233.md) into [#233](../issues/DOT-232.md); [#241](../issues/DOT-240.md) into [#459](../issues/DOT-430.md) (both are one line in the same block of `git_config`); [#282](../issues/DOT-281.md) into [#720](../issues/DOT-485.md); [#286](../issues/DOT-285.md) into [#461](../issues/DOT-431.md); [#477](../issues/DOT-435.md) into [#419](../issues/DOT-409.md) (the answer is `~/.ssh/config`, not a shell hook); [#665](../issues/DOT-483.md) into [#664](../issues/DOT-482.md).
4. **Decide the alias question before refactoring aliases.** [#355](../issues/DOT-354.md) and its six children ([#356](../issues/DOT-355.md)–[#361](../issues/DOT-360.md)) assume the commands they move still exist. Half of them are registered only by `bin/legacy/git` and are therefore absent on every current machine — including `root` and `url`, which [#288](../issues/DOT-287.md) and [#421](../issues/DOT-411.md) build on. The first decision is which of those commands are wanted at all; migration or deletion follows from it, and [#360](../issues/DOT-359.md) is very likely deletion.
5. **Fix the three confirmed defects, which are cheap and are not really features.** The remote-branch split in `git_shake` ([#160](../issues/DOT-159.md), also inherited by [#359](../issues/DOT-358.md)); the explicit `--tags` in `git-pull` that overrides `tagopt` ([#637](../issues/DOT-478.md)); and `gum` being undeclared while `books` depends on it ([#556](../issues/DOT-459.md), [#626](../issues/DOT-476.md)) — one Brewfile line or one guard.
6. **Treat `self-update` and `install` as one piece of work.** [#558](../issues/DOT-460.md) and [#725](../issues/DOT-487.md) hold six findings between them — `eval` dispatch, an unconditional `git reset --hard`, a wildcard delete of the shared Go bin directory, a top-level `return`, a zsh builtin called from bash, an SSH-only clone. [#399](../issues/DOT-397.md) (a VM test) is what would have caught all six, and [#172](../issues/DOT-171.md) (migrations) is what the blunt substitutes stand in for. These four should be scheduled together or not at all.
7. **Restate six issues that are specified against a world that changed.** [#232](../issues/DOT-231.md) — the GPG path is done, the remaining scope is SSH signing; [#376](../issues/DOT-375.md) — it names `maintainer` subcommands that do not exist; [#377](../issues/DOT-376.md) — the crash is fixed, what is left is a design question and the `type: bug` label is now wrong; [#481](../issues/DOT-437.md) — same problem, `maintainer` flags have moved; [#375](../issues/DOT-374.md) — the inventory it extends stopped being maintained in 2023; [#600](../issues/DOT-464.md) — Warp is adopted, powerlevel10k is not, and one ticket cannot be half closed.
8. **Settle the runtime-management question once.** [#461](../issues/DOT-431.md), [#471](../issues/DOT-434.md) and [#272](../issues/DOT-271.md) are three answers to "how are language runtimes managed", and [#162](../issues/DOT-161.md) only exists because the answer is currently "globally, by hand". One decision closes or reframes four issues.
9. **Finish the classification that [#302](../issues/DOT-301.md) started.** The prefix convention and the label scheme hold for newer issues, but 66 of the 116 open issues carry no labels at all, and [#471](../issues/DOT-434.md) carries two contradictory `effort` values. The dump plus these reviews are the working form of that ticket; labelling the open set is what is left of it.

These are recommendations, and none of them was acted on. No issue was closed, reopened, relabelled or retitled. The changes made were: the descriptions in `.github/issues/` reduced to intent, the comment threads mirrored in both directions between GitHub and the dump, seventy-nine new comments published, and this file written.

## Comments

Observations that belong to one issue rather than to this review are kept as `<!-- ISO-8601 timestamp, comment URL -->` blocks at the end of the issue file, in chronological order. That set is now a two-way mirror of the comment threads: GitHub holds 219 comments across 178 issues, the dump holds 219 notes across 178 files, and they match one to one by URL with identical bodies.

Of those, seventy-nine were written and published during this pass. 138 are older comments, going back to 2018, that the export had never carried; they are imported verbatim, which is why a file may now open with a 2018 remark by the author and close with a 2026 one. Two notes that paraphrased comments already on GitHub were replaced by the text of those comments.

The one deliberate divergence is redaction: three imported comments quoted a home directory, which reads `/Users/.../` here as it does everywhere else in the dump, and one quoted an installer line naming the local account. Host names were left alone — the repository already carries them as Brewfile names.

Three notes were added by this review, for findings that belong to a single issue rather than to the backlog as a whole: the plugin removal that partly undid [#114](../issues/DOT-113.md), the inverted guard in [#67](../issues/DOT-66.md), and the contradictory `effort` labels on [#471](../issues/DOT-434.md).

Where a note was written for the local dump it now reads as it does on GitHub: cross-references use issue numbers rather than file names, review findings name the review file, and two notes were reworded — one dropped a former employer's internal host name, the other an example of a shell-injection payload. Neither belongs on a public tracker, and neither was needed to make the point.
